role_title: Federal entry-level land-management technicians and student trainees (GS-0462/0404/0499)
description: 2025 hiring freeze, probationary firings and no non-fire seasonal hiring cut the federal entry rung; 2,000 seasonals restored in 2026; under-30 share 7.9%; student trainee occupations down. Driver is fiscal/policy, not AI; v1 CLD logic attributes ladder risk to automation only

role_title: Early-career analysts in high-LLM-exposure environmental occupations (environmental specialists, planners, compliance and sustainability analysts)
description: Env analytical occupations sit at the 90th-99th exposure percentile; private payroll evidence shows 22-25-year-olds in top-exposure quintiles ~19% below counterfactual by June 2026 via reduced hiring. No environment-specific employment evidence exists yet; ADP undercovers government

role_title: Environmental review and NEPA document specialists
description: Enterprise genAI drafting/summarizing tools are available near agency-wide at EPA (10,000-50,000 users) and DOI/USDA (50,000+ for some tools) while custom NEPA/permitting AI remains pilot or pre-deployment (5 cases, 0 deployed). NEPA procedure changes (SC) shorten documents and timelines. Task compression is plausible; staffing effect unobserved

role_title: Wildland fire operations and management positions
description: DOI fire programs consolidated into the U.S. Wildland Fire Service (Jan 2026) with aligned USWFS/USFS qualification standards due Jan 2027; wildland fire management series grew while other land-management occupations fell

role_title: Forest plan monitoring coordinators and resource data stewards
description: 2012-rule plans devote 22% of components to monitoring (median 34 per plan) vs 1.8% in 1982-rule plans; 1,506 monitoring questions across 45 plans; reporting/data-system language is the most-named method (16% of questions). Demand is for indicator design, evaluation reporting and data stewardship rather than for specific field methods

role_title: Partnership, cross-boundary and Tribal coordination roles
description: Per 1,000 components, 2012-rule plans name partnership touchpoints 31.4 vs 10.0 (1982 rule), Tribal 27.3 vs 10.0, cross-boundary 13.8 vs 4.5; USFS reorganization expands states' role (via AS). GNA/shared stewardship rarely appear in plan text (21 components) because they operate through agreements

role_title: Geospatial, remote-sensing and environmental data analysts in science bureaus
description: Of 504 AI use cases in environmental bureaus, 232 are classical ML; remote sensing/imagery (63; 11 deployed), species detection (89; 11 deployed) and hydrology (36; 10 deployed) dominate. AI is entering the analysis pipeline, mostly pre-deployment/pilot

role_title: Field survey biologists and technicians (species and habitat surveys)
description: Sensor-based detection (acoustic, camera, eDNA, imagery) is the main technology vector for field surveys, but plans rarely name methods (remote sensing in 3 monitoring questions, eDNA in 3). Method change will appear in protocols, PDs and postings, not plans; no index measures this sensing-substitution vector

role_title: Corporate sustainability and GHG/ESG reporting analysts
description: Sustainability Specialists are at the 97th exposure percentile; large-firm functions report growth (46%) more than cuts (25%) and higher compliance priority. Disclosure-rule volatility, not AI, is the dominant short-run driver

role_title: Senior scientific and technical staff in regulatory agencies (EPA and similar)
description: EPA staffing at 40-year lows; departing staff median tenure ~30 years vs ~11 years for those remaining (via FS). This removes the top of the ladder - the reviewers who certify AI-compressed work - a CLD mechanism v1 does not model
Park rangers -34.1% (via PPS/FH). v1 records a High CLD on 5.5.1 T1 (visitor services) attributed to AI compression; the observed decline is fiscal/policy-driven

Recreation is the largest theme in plan standards (3,819 components, 15%) and monitoring questions (17%); ROS and scenery classifications appear in 62 and 68 plans; special-use authorizations 363 touchpoints. v1 has no recreation planning or travel management competency

Lowest usage-based AI applicability of any env occupation (0.6th pct) and 75% physical tasks; change vector is SCADA/automation and cybersecurity, not LLMs; v1 has no water-utility competencies (audit)
